title: Introduction to Stepper Motors
summary: From serial commands to stepper motor motion using Arduino IDE, LabVIEW, and VISA.
**Central question:** How does a typed command from LabVIEW become controlled stepper motor motion through Arduino firmware?
cardSummary: Stepper motor fundamentals, external power setup, motor driver wiring, Arduino IDE firmware upload, Serial Monitor tests, LabVIEW VISA serial commands, and angle-control extension.

checkpoints.title: Scenario and objectives
intro: You are building a local motion-control node that receives commands from a LabVIEW HMI, sends those commands over serial to Arduino firmware, and uses a motor driver plus external power supply to move a stepper motor in controlled increments.

blocks.alt: Stepper motor model with windings and a permanent-magnet rotor.
blocks.caption: Stepper motor model: energized windings act on the permanent-magnet rotor.

blocks.alt: Four winding states that produce stepper motor motion.
blocks.caption: Sequential winding states produce controlled, incremental shaft steps.

blocks.title: Learning goals
items: Build and drive a stepper motor with Arduino and LabVIEW.
Compile and upload Arduino firmware.
Send and parse serial data between LabVIEW and Arduino.
Explain the motor driver and external power supply.

blocks.title: Warning
paragraphs: The stepper motor may heat up during operation. This can be normal, but use caution before touching the motor after it has been energized.

items.label: Arduino IDE is installed.

blocks.title: If power or motion is abnormal
paragraphs: Switch off the external supply before touching wiring. Recheck 9 V adaptor selection, power-board polarity, regulated rails, common ground, and the D8-D11 to IN1-IN4 mapping before powering again.

checkpoints.title: Compile and upload the Arduino firmware

blocks.alt: Arduino IDE with stepper motor firmware.
blocks.caption: Create a new sketch, paste the provided firmware, verify it, and upload it to the Arduino Mega.

paragraphs: The firmware uses the standard Arduino `Stepper.h` library, initializes serial communication at 9600 baud, reads a command string until newline, parses comma-separated values, and commands the stepper motor.

blocks.title: Provided stepper firmware
Required actions
items: Open Arduino IDE and create a new sketch.
Paste the provided code.
Select Tools - Board - Arduino Mega.
Select the correct Tools - Port.
Click Verify and resolve compile errors.
Click Upload to load firmware.

checkpoints.title: Test command parsing with Arduino Serial Monitor

blocks.alt: Arduino Serial Monitor for sending stepper motor commands.
blocks.caption: Set the baud rate to 9600, enter a command such as `10,1.5,1`, and send it to the Arduino.

paragraphs: Use the syntax `RPM,Number Revolutions,Direction`. For example, `10,1.5,1` requests 10 RPM, 1.5 revolutions, and clockwise direction.
Close the Serial Monitor before running the LabVIEW VI. By default, only one client can use the same serial port at one time.

blocks.summary: If a Serial Monitor command does not produce safe motion
paragraphs: Stop sending commands and switch off motor power if the motor stalls, locks, or becomes hot. Verify 9600 baud, two comma delimiters, the newline setting, direction as 1 or -1, and a conservative RPM before changing one item and retesting.

checkpoints.title: Use LabVIEW VISA Serial to write commands

blocks.alt: LabVIEW block diagram with serial configuration, buffer, write, close, while loop, wait, and case structure.
blocks.caption: Configure the serial port, use a loop and Case Structure, and close VISA after the loop.

blocks.alt: Complete LabVIEW block diagram with string concatenation, number conversion, direction selection, sent-message indicator, VISA Write, and close functions.
blocks.caption: Concatenate RPM, a comma, revolutions, a comma, and direction into the string written to Arduino.

paragraphs: Add Configure Port, Set Buffer Size, Write, and Close from Data Communication - Protocols - Serial. Set VISA Resource Name to the Arduino serial port.
Use the Message Arduino button to decide whether to build and send a command string. In the false case, carry wires through.
Use five inputs: RPM string, comma, Revolutions, comma, Direction string.
Change the RPM meter from Indicator to Control and wire it through Number to Decimal String.
Use Select to output string constant `1` for clockwise and `-1` for counter-clockwise.
Close Arduino Serial Monitor, run the VI, send commands, and observe motor motion.

blocks.summary: If Serial Monitor works but LabVIEW VISA does not
paragraphs: Close Serial Monitor, verify the VISA Resource Name, confirm the command contains both commas and the required line ending, and check that VISA Write is in the True case. Keep the proven firmware and hardware unchanged while testing one LabVIEW correction at a time.

checkpoints.title: Replace revolutions with an angle command
intro: Replace the Revolutions control with an Angle control. Instead of entering 0.5, 1, or 2 revolutions, the user enters 180, 360, or 720 degrees.

paragraphs: Convert angle to revolutions in LabVIEW before concatenating the serial string.

items.description: A motor that moves in discrete angular increments called steps.
Torque available when the shaft is not rotating but energized coils resist movement.
Interface circuit that supplies motor current and switches coils based on Arduino control signals.
Separate power source used because the motor needs more current than Arduino should supply.
Regulated board that provides the 5 V rail used by the motor driver in this lab.
Shared 0 V reference between Arduino and motor driver circuit.
Arduino library used to command stepper motor speed and steps.
Number of motor steps used in the sketch for one full revolution: 2048.
Arduino IDE tool used to send typed serial commands to Arduino.
LabVIEW communication functions used to configure, write to, and close a serial port.
A character such as a comma used to separate fields in a command string.
Revolutions per minute, used as the stepper speed command.
Command field where 1 indicates clockwise and -1 indicates counter-clockwise.
Program uploaded to Arduino to parse commands and actuate the motor.
Finer step control achieved by partially energizing the windings; it is included here for optional exploration.
